title: Chapter II: A Tribute
text:
Chapter II

A Tribute

To Robert Rebecca Halsell, President of Savoy College 1880-1888, who never turned away a boy or girl, no matter how poor, who wanted an education.
(Published in the Savoy Rustler, December, 1948.)

As I stood upon the platform at the recent reunion of Ex-Students of Savoy College and gazed upon a sea of faces, my memory slipped back quickly over the years—many, many years—and I saw distinctly in the background another scene, which time has failed to dim for me.

Time—the old bell had just summoned the happy student body for the opening exercises, and a host of young men, young women, boys and girls, with eager eyes and listening ears, were facing the faculty on the platform. A chorus of "Good Morning" was rendered; a scripture reading was offered, after which Robert Rebecca Halsell, president and spark plug of this educational institution, stepped forward and began in his own inimitable way—

"Young ladies and young gentlemen, we are face to face with another week of hard work and progress, and Savoy College expects every one to do his duty."

Our hearts were strangely warmed and our enthusiasm began to bristle. Then he told us in effect, to take a strong rope, tie one end to our wagon, hitch the other to a star, and—

Climb!
Climb!

The occasion was typical. Often at such times he would take up a famous painting or a model, and with a few extra touches, mold it into a model that any boy could admire; he glad to emulate.
